headline: 28 trades net -2.1 bps/bet (-60 bps total); rolling-9 window +10.1 bps net, but sample far too thin to judge.
regime_note: BTC ~$76.4k, in the upper $76-81k band where recent short-side fades have resolved favorably; the loss-heavy cluster sits earlier around $63-66k. Signal is flat (0), so nothing is live right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Over the full live ledger of 28 resolved trades, the strategy is net **-2.1 bps/bet (-60 bps total)** with a **35.7% win rate**. That is below breakeven — unsurprising, since this signal was flagged from the start as marginal (gross edge ~4 bps vs ~3.9 bps breakeven cost). The rolling recent window (9 bets) looks better: **+10.1 bps net, 66.7% wins**, but that's driven by a few outsized winners (+48.7, +25.9, +16.2 bps) rather than broad consistency.

**What changed since last time.** Only one new trade resolved (Sep 17, -4.0 bps). The overall ledger drifted from -56 to -60 bps total; the recent-window positivity persists but on an even smaller count. Nothing structural changed.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** With 28 trades total — and a selective signal that trades ~1-2% of candles — this is nowhere near enough to conclude the edge is real *or* dead. The P&L is dominated by a handful of large moves (the +52 and -28 bps trades swing the whole picture). A negative full-sample mean is consistent with both 'no edge' and 'thin, noisy edge.' Note also `edge_search_survivors: 0` at the 5 bps bar — the offline search found nothing clearing realistic costs.

**Bottom line.** Behaving roughly as expected for a marginal signal: slightly net-negative overall, noisy, sample too small to act on. No degradation alert warranted, but no evidence of durable profit either. Keep collecting data; do not expect this to be reliably net-profitable after costs.
